title: indian shares likely rebound after recent slide higher oil prices cap upside 2026 09 03
text:
Sept 3 (Reuters) - Indian benchmark equities were subdued on Thursday, with the Nifty closing largely flat as risk aversion sparked by elevated ​oil prices outweighed gains in banking stocks following the central bank's stronger-than-expected ‌dollar mobilisation.
The BSE Sensex (.BSESN)
, opens new tab
 plunged as much as 2.5% during the closing auction, with the index extending losses on weekly derivatives expiry as volatility during the closing auction intensified.
The Nifty 50 (.NSEI)
, opens new tab
 fell 0.17% to ​23,873.45 and the Sensex shed 0.55% to 76,152.86 at the close.
The Nifty ​and Sensex were down 0.04% and 0.02%, ahead of the ⁠closing auction session.
The closing auction session is already reshaping options trading, prompting participants to ​trim positions and ramp up hedges as wild swings in the final 15 minutes ​make closing levels increasingly difficult to call.
The benchmarks had lost about 1% each over the past three sessions, pressured by climbing crude prices and rising global bond yields.
Brent crude rose ​1% to $96.6 a barrel after renewed military strikes between the U.S. and Iran ​intensified inflationary, energy supply worries.
Nine of the 16 major sectors declined. Banks (.NSEBANK)
, opens new tab
, financials (.NIFTYFIN)
, opens new tab
, private lenders (.NIFPVTBNK)
, opens new tab
 and state-owned ‌banks (.NIFTYPSU)
, opens new tab
 ⁠climbed between 0.3% and 0.6%.
Banks mobilized more than $60 billion in deposits from non-resident Indians during the final 10 days of the RBI's swap scheme, taking total inflows to $136 billion.
"These inflows bolster bank liquidity, opening more runway for credit growth across ​the system as ​we head to ⁠the festive season," said Kranthi Bathini, director of equity strategy at Wealthmills Securities.
"However, benchmark indices remain range-bound despite the domestic ​growth data and the liquidity boost as crude remains the ​joker in ⁠the pack for inflation, global bond yields and the durability of domestic demand," Bathini said.
Small-caps (.NIFSMCP100)
, opens new tab
 and mid-caps (.NIFMDCP100)
, opens new tab
 gained 1.2% and 0.4%, buoyed by earnings visibility, domestic inflows and ⁠diversification.
Consumer ​company Godrej Consumer (GOCP.NS)
, opens new tab
 fell 2.8% after multiple brokerages ​projected near-term pressure due to sustained palm oil inflation.
IT company Hexaware (HEXW.NS)
, opens new tab
 fell 2.1% after its CEO's exit spurred concerns ​over the growth outlook.
